title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 121
paragraphs: Afterwards, however, the Carians repaired this loss and retrieved their defeat. For being informed that the Persians had set out to march against their cities, they laid an ambush on the road that runs by Pedasus; and the Persians, falling into it by night, were destroyed—both they and their commanders, namely Daurises and Amorges and Sisimaces; and with them died Myrsus son of Gyges as well. The leader of this ambush was Heraclides son of Ibanollis, a man of Mylasa.
